scope: Corollary 1.2 (Tensor products and stable finiteness) of the manuscript “A counterexample to Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture and failure of tensor-product stable finiteness” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-quasitrace-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 294 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c46465adfaef9b9f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: (i) There are two unital simple stably finite complex C∗-algebras whose minimal tensor product is properly infinite. One factor can be taken to be C∗ r (F2). (ii) There is a separable unital complex C∗-algebra B admitting a normalized 2-quasitrace such that B ⊗min C∗ r (F2) is properly infinite and admits no normalized 2-quasitrace. (iii) There is a separable unital stably finite complex C∗-algebra with no tracial state.
